examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Cardinality of a Power Set
examples.worked_solution:
For any set $Y,$ we have $\left|\mathcal{P}(Y)\right| = 2^{\left| Y \right|}.$

In this case, $\left| Y \right| = 4,$ so we have

$$
\left| \mathcal{P}(Y) \right| = 2^{\left| Y \right|} = 2^{4} = 16.
$$

Remember that $\{ 3,5 \}$ is a single element in the set $Y.$

The power set of $S,$ denoted $P(S),$ is the set that contains every possible subset of $S,$ including the empty set $∅.$

So, let's list all possible subsets of $S$ using a tree diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14098182/assets/c02cab907b20d7c740c0f31d5474564eb24a43a9b89667d3a0093d8242597405.png)

According to our diagram, the subsets of $S$ are

$$
∅={},\,{a},\,{b},\,{a,b}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
P(S)={∅,{a},{b},{a,b}}.
$$
